bw: Anterior shoulder dislocation, humeral head below coracoid
w: The Neer impingement test assesses rotator cuff impingement and is not done on a dislocated shoulder.
The drop arm test evaluates supraspinatus tears, not nerve injury from dislocation.
p: Document neurovascular status, especially axillary nerve sensation over the lateral deltoid, before and after reducing an anterior shoulder dislocation.

bw: Anterior thigh numbness, worse when standing
w: Lumbar MRI is unnecessary because the straight leg test and strength are normal and the sign points to the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.
Reducing physical activity does not address the mechanical nerve compression.
p: Meralgia paresthetica: lateral femoral cutaneous nerve compression at the inguinal ligament from tight clothing, obesity or pregnancy; avoid compression.

w: Bacillus cereus causes vomiting or diarrhea after reheated rice, not seafood.
Rotavirus causes watery diarrhea in children and is not bloody.
p: Vibrio parahaemolyticus causes gastroenteritis after raw or undercooked shellfish; V. vulnificus causes wound infection and sepsis in liver disease.

w: Tinnitus and hearing loss follow cisplatin or aminoglycosides.
Hemorrhagic cystitis with hematuria follows cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide.
p: Anthracyclines (doxorubicin, daunorubicin) cause dilated cardiomyopathy via free radical injury; dexrazoxane is cardioprotective.

bw: Child with periorbital swelling, then anasarca
w: Acute glomerulonephritis presents with hematuria, hypertension and RBC casts rather than massive proteinuria.
Protein-losing enteropathy does not cause heavy proteinuria with fatty casts.
p: Minimal change disease is the most common childhood nephrotic syndrome: effaced podocyte foot processes on EM, responds to steroids.

x: unclear first-step choice in metabolic confusion
